item.title: Hybrid mechanics of coupled qubits
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
We find that a technique analogous to hybrid mechanics previously developed for Gaussian coherent states and molecular vibrations, can be extended to SU(2) coherent states describing coupled qubits. This formulation reveals a sparse structure of the propagator, leading to a computationally efficient scheme while maintaining numerical accuracy. As a result, the method enables simulations of larger qubit systems on classical computers. In particular, we demonstrate accurate real-time propagation for systems of up to 21 qubits, which would be computationally demanding using straightforward quantum-dynamics approaches.

item.title: Position-and conformation-dependent effects of fluorination on the structure and methyl internal rotation of methyl benzoates
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
The effects of fluorination on molecular structure and internal dynamics were investigated in monofluorinated methyl benzoates (methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, methyl 3-fluorobenzoate, and methyl 4-fluorobenzoate) using high-resolution rotational spectroscopy in combination with quantum-chemical calculations. Two conformers were identified for methyl 2-fluorobenzoate, whereas only one conformer each was observed for the 3- and 4-fluorinated species. All observed conformers exhibited A / E torsional splittings arising from internal rotation of the ester methyl rotor and were analyzed using the XIAM code. item.title: Quantum Spherical Fuzzy Decision Framework with Golden Cut and ARTASI for Sustainable Mining Method Selection in Geologically Complex Thin Seams
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Nidahamteinsar Papang, Bishal Gurung, Priya Sharma
The selection of a suitable mining method for geologically complex and thin coal seams, particularly those with thicknesses ranging from 0.30 to 2.12 m, remains a critical challenge. In Meghalaya, this issue is of paramount importance, as conventional unscientific extraction practices have been associated with safety hazards, resource losses, and environmental degradation. This study proposes a Quantum Spherical Fuzzy Large-Scale Decision-Making (QSF-LSDM) framework to support the systematic selection of mining methods under uncertain and conflicting conditions. item.title: Regulation, function and evolutionary structure of St18, encoding a Zinc-Finger Transcription Factor, in the oligodendrocyte lineage
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 David Rowitch, Daniel Yamamoto, Adrien Vaquié, Tim Aberle, Michael Perry, Davod Shah 等21位作者
Myelinating oligodendrocytes are first observed during evolution in vertebrates above jawless fishes. Oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) undergo extensive transcriptional and morphological remodelling to initiate differentiation and myelination. We report that the zinc-finger transcription factor St18 (aka Myt3) is upregulated during the OPC-to–newly formed oligodendrocyte (NFOL) transition. Single-nucleus RNA-sequencing (snRNA-seq) performed after lysolecithin-induced demyelination of the mouse spinal cord revealed that St18 was acutely upregulated in remyelinating OPCs. In primary rat OPC cultures, St18 overexpression promoted differentiation, whereas OPC conditional St18 knockout delayed developmental myelination in the mouse brain. item.title: Rovibrational cross sections for the CO 2 00 0 0, 01 1 0, 02 2 0, and Fermi resonance states 10 0 0(1) and 10 0 0(2) in collisions with He atoms
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
We present quantum scattering calculations of CO 2 –He state-to-state integral cross sections for 25 transition sets, covering pure rotational transitions within and rovibrational transitions between: the ground state 00 0 0, the bend fundamental 01 1 0, the bending overtone 02 2 0, and the Fermi doublet states 10 0 0(1) and 10 0 0(2). Exact coupled-channel (CC) and coupled-states approximation (CSA) calculations are performed using a new five-dimensional potential energy surface. The calculations cover collision energies from 20 to 5220 cm −1 , sufficient to obtain converged rate coefficients over 100–800 K, and include initial rotational states for each transition up to at least j = 35. item.title: Slow-motion electron camera reveals light-driven quantum jumps in graphene
item.description:
📚 Physics News
Using a new slow-motion electron camera, physicists from Regensburg, Marburg and Jülich revealed how intense electric fields drive electrons in graphene, causing them to jump across energy gaps in a seemingly paradoxical manner. This was made possible by a novel combination of laser technology and electron microscopy.

item.title: Third-order size-consistent Brillouin–Wigner perturbation theory
item.description:
📚 The Journal of Chemical Physics Current Issue
Low-order Rayleigh–Schrödinger perturbation theory with Møller–Plesset partitioning is size-consistent but not regular, and for this reason, the third-order variant, MP3, is not commonly used in computational quantum chemistry. item.title: Trainable, self-verifying variational quantum eigensolver using adiabatic warm starts
item.description:
📚 Phys. Rev. Research
👤 Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, and Michael Lubasch
Author(s): Bojan Žunkovič, Marco Ballarin, Lewis Wright, and Michael Lubasch A study looks at the conditions under which an adiabatic variational quantum eigensolver succeeds, where approximate ground states generated along an adiabatic path serve as initial states for successive optimization steps. A self-verification procedure based on energy-standard-deviation measurements is introduced that assesses eigenstate accuracy during run-time and verifies convergence to the target ground state. item.title: Self-Calibrated Hyperspectral Neural Radiance Fields for 3D Reconstruction of Bone and Bone Analogues
item.description:
📚 Preprints
👤 Neetu Sigger, Tuan Thanh Nguyen, Sadaf Ashraf, Gianluca Tozzi
Hyperspectral imaging (HSI) captures rich, wavelength-dependent information linked to mineralised tissue composition, while3D reconstruction preserves surface morphology and structural detail. Combining the two offers a powerful, non-contactapproach for bone assessment, yet existing hyperspectral 3D reconstruction methods rely on externally estimated cameraposes (e.g., via COLMAP), an assumption that is often unreliable on bone surfaces due to their low texture, specular reflectance,and irregular morphology. To address this challenge, we propose BoNeRF-HS, a self-calibrated hyperspectral neural radiancefield for 3D reconstruction. item.description:

👤 Joan Carles Martori, Raymond Lagonigro
The commemoration of the 150th anniversary of Ildefons Cerdà’s death during the Cerdà Year 2026, together with Barcelona’s designation as World Capital of Architecture 2026, provides a timely context in which to reassess the contemporary relevance of Cerdà’s urban principles.
